remedy_text: A decoction (Kashaya) is defined as a preparation where medicinal herbs are boiled with sixteen parts of water until reduced to one-fourth. Its administration is strictly forbidden during the early stage of acute fever.

remedy_text: (Dry Fomentation / Valuka Sveda): Therapy: In Vata-Kapha fevers, dry hot sand fomentation (Valuka Sveda) must be applied. ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: In Vata-Kapha fever, dry sudation (Ruksha Sveda) must be applied first. By softening the channels (Srotas) and guiding the internal digestive fire back to the visceral tract (Kostha), sudation breaks up the combined rigidity of Vata and Kapha and roots out the fever.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: Fomentation using a heated sand poultice (Valuka Sveda)-prepared by filling clean sand into a broken earthen pot shard, warming it over fire, and wrapping it in cloth-promptly dispels Vata-Kapha disorders, intense headaches, and splitting pain in the joints.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

Preparation & Dose: Take two masha (~2 grams) of each, boil down in eight pala (~380 ml) of water to one-fourth, cool, and stir in half a pala (~24 grams) of pure honey.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Administered at intervals of one muhurta (approx. 48 minutes), this decoction destroys fever without a doubt.. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: Sannipata cannot be pacified without sudation (Svedana); hence fomentation must be applied repeatedly. In Sannipata, the body channels are clogged with fluid and cold mucus; without the agency of therapeutic heat, how could those soggy channels be dried? Even the most toxic mineral remedies fail to show their therapeutic potency without the kindle of metabolic heat.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Maheshvara Dhupa Action): In whatever home this incense is burned, snakes never linger, evil spirits and demons flee, and quotidian, tertian, and quartan fevers are dispelled without fail. While offering it onto hot coals, recite: "Om namo bhagavate rudraya umapataye sasainyaya nandikeshvaraya svaha."
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Indications for Medicated Ghee / Ghrita): When a patient with a dry, unctuous-depleted constitution (Ruksha Deha) finds no relief from decoctions, emesis, fasting, or light diets, the physician must administer medicated clarified butter (Ghrita).

condition_name: Pitta Fever, High Thirst & Burning Sensation
remedy_text: (Pippalyadi Ghrita): Ingredients: Pippali, red sandalwood, Musta, Ushira, Kutki, Indrayava, Bhumiamalaki, Sariva, Ativisha, Shalaparni, Draksha, Amalaki, Neem, Trayamana, and Kantakari. Indication: Cooked with clarified butter, this medicated ghee cures chronic lingering fevers, phthisis/consumption (Kshaya), dyspnea, headaches, flank pain, loss of appetite, burning limbs, and irregular digestion.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Cooked with clarified butter, this medicated ghee cures chronic lingering fevers, phthisis/consumption (Kshaya), dyspnea. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Kshirashatpala Ghrita): Ingredients: Panchakola herbs (Pippali, Pippalimula, Chavya, Chitraka, Nagara) and Saindhava (rock salt), one pala (~48 g) each; cook in one prastha (~640 ml) of ghee along with equal parts of milk. Indication: Destroys intermittent fevers and abdominal phantom tumors (Gulma).
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Destroys intermittent fevers and abdominal phantom tumors (Gulma).. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Dashamula Shatpala Ghrita): Dashamula decoction, milk, ghee, Panchakola herbs, and Yavakshara cooked together; this medicated ghee cures chronic fevers, cough, low digestion, tridoshic disorders, splenomegaly, and severe anemia (Pandu).
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: cures chronic fevers, cough, low digestion, tridoshic disorders, splenomegaly, and severe anemia (Pandu). Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Mahasudarshana Churna Ingredients): Take equal parts of: Aguru, Haridra, Devadaru, Vacha, Musta, Haritaki, Dhanvayasa, Karkatashringi, Kantakari, dry ginger, Trayamana, Parpataka, Neem bark, Pippalimula, Netrabala, Kachura, Pushkaramula, Pippali, Murva, Kutaja bark, licorice, Maricha, Indrayava, Shatavari, Daruharidra, red sandalwood, Padmaka, Sarala, Ushira, Dalchini, Saurashtri (alum), Rasna, Shalaparni, Ajwain, Ativisha, Bilva, black pepper, .
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Angaraka Taila): Ingredients: Murva, Laksha, Haridra, Daruharidra, Manjistha, Indravaruni, Brihati, Saindhava (rock salt), Kushta, Rasna, Jatamansi, and Shatavari. Preparation: Cook in one adhaka (~2.5 liters) of sour fermented gruel (Aranala) and one prastha (~640 ml) of sesame oil. Indication: Named Angaraka Taila, this oil destroys all varieties of fever through external massage.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Named Angaraka Taila, this oil destroys all varieties of fever through external massage.. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Brihadangaraka Taila): Prepared with the Angaraka herbs along with dry radish (Shushka Mulaka), Eranda root, and four parts water; this oil dispels obstinate fevers, inflammatory edema, and severe anemia.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

condition_name: Pitta Fever, High Thirst & Burning Sensation
remedy_text: (Lakshadi Taila): Cook sesame oil with Laksha (lac), Haridra, and Manjistha in six parts sour gruel (Aranala); massaged over the body, it relieves fever accompanied by intense burning heat and swelling.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Brihat Lakshadi Taila): Take one adhaka of Laksha decoction, one prastha of sesame oil, and one adhaka of yogurt whey (Mastu). Add a paste of: Shatapushpa, Haridra, Murva, Kushta, Renuka, Kutki, licorice, Rasna, Devadaru, Musta, and red sandalwood.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Kattara Taila): Ingredients: Sauvarcala salt, dry ginger, Kushta, Murva, Laksha, Haridra, and Manjistha. Preparation: Cook in sesame oil with six parts sour churned buttermilk (Kattara Takra). Indication: Massaged over the body, it kindles digestive fire and terminates Vata-Kapha fever, quotidian, tertian, quartan, and fevers returning every fortnight or month.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Massaged over the body, it kindles digestive fire and terminates Vata-Kapha fever, quotidian, tertian, quartan, and feve. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Shatkattaka Taila): Cook sesame oil with sour gruel, yogurt, whey, buttermilk, and citrus fruit juice in equal proportions, adding a fine paste of the Pippalyadi herbs; this massage subdues Vata-Kapha fevers.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: subdues Vata-Kapha fevers. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: This great oil (Shatkattaka Taila) terminates intermittent fevers returning daily, on alternate days, every fourth day, every fortnight, every month, or every two months.
ayurvedic_note: Classical formulation from Ayurveda treatise. Action: Fever and associated clinical symptoms. Balances somatic humors and cleanses metabolic waste (Ama).

remedy_text: (Brihat Pippalyadi Taila Ingredients & Method): Ingredients: Pippali, Musta, coriander, Saindhava (rock salt), Triphala, Vacha, Ajwain, Ajamoda, red sandalwood, Pushkaramula, Kachura, raisins, Indravaruni, Shalaparni, Gokshura, Chirayata, Neem leaves, Mahanimba, Kantakari, Giloy, Prishniparni, Brihati, Danti, Chitraka, Daruharidra, Haridra, Chavya, Parpataka, and Gajapippali.
